correctness.rationale: The type-D spin orbit is exactly one parity class of the half-cube vertices. The standard parity-polytope H-description gives coordinate facets at distance 1/2 and parity-simplex facets at distance (n-2)/(2 sqrt(n)). The latter equals 1/2 only at n=4 and is larger for n>=5. Opposite coordinate facets force any optimal radius-1/2 center to be zero. All vertices have norm sqrt(n)/2, and Weyl invariance plus uniqueness forces the circumcenter to zero. Uniqueness of John and Löwner ellipsoids makes them Weyl-invariant; signed-permutation invariance forces a scalar quadratic form, so they are exactly the inball and circumball.

value.rationale: The spin fundamental-weight polytopes are distinguished indecomposable rays in the symmetric Coxeter deformation theory, while the same bodies are classical demihypercubes and parity polytopes. The result connects these three settings by a complete Euclidean extremal-ellipsoid profile, not just a single radius: unique centers, exact John and Löwner ellipsoids, a sharp change in the active facet orbit at n=4, all outer contact points, and equality in the sqrt(n) John containment scale. This is an all-dimensional structural metric classification of a canonical Coxeter family rather than a finite table or arbitrary slice.
